[Step 04] Learn the instrument’s basic terminology and layout. Identify its parts and how notes are produced. Use diagrams, audio, or demonstrations rather than sheet music.

[Step 06] Learn basic technique through short exercises. Practice one small skill at a time, such as pressing a key cleanly, changing chords, picking a string, or keeping a steady beat. Use slow demonstrations and copy them by ear or by watching.

[Step 07] Choose a simple song you enjoy and can learn without sheet music. Find a beginner tutorial, chord chart, tablature, numbered-key guide, or recording with clear demonstrations. Check that the version matches your instrument and skill level.

[Step 08] Break the song into small sections. Learn one phrase or chord change at a time, first slowly, then connect the sections. Repeat difficult transitions separately instead of restarting the whole song.

[Step 09] Practice with a steady pulse. Use a metronome, drum loop, or backing track at a comfortable tempo. Increase the speed gradually only when you can play the section accurately several times in a row.

[Step 10] Experiment with simple melodies. Hum or listen to a short phrase, then find its notes by trial and error, using your instrument’s layout or a tutorial as a guide. Record yourself and compare what you played with the phrase you intended.

[Step 11] Follow a repeatable practice routine. Start with a few minutes of warm-up, spend most of the session on one focused skill or song section, then finish by playing something enjoyable. Begin with manageable sessions, such as 15–20 minutes, several times a week.

[Step 12] Track progress and adjust your next session. Note what you practiced, what improved, and what remains difficult. If you feel pain, stop and check your technique; if you feel stuck, slow down, simplify the passage, or seek feedback from a teacher or experienced player.

[Step 13] Once you can play a few pieces comfortably, choose a next goal, such as learning a new song, improving timing, playing with a recording, or learning basic music notation if you decide it would be useful."}
